proposals.announcement_evidence: to exercise options for in-Service AEGIS combat system baseline sustainment, Baseline 10 System Integration and Fielding, and product documentation
proposals.lexicon_quote: The AEGIS Combat System (ACS)	0604307N	340	Surface Combatant Combat System Engineering
proposals.rationale: The announcement names the AEGIS combat system verbatim (the index row differs only by its leading article and trailing acronym), and the scope is not platform support but the combat system's own engineering: in-service baseline sustainment plus 'Baseline 10 System Integration and Fielding' and product documentation, performed by Lockheed Martin at Moorestown, the AEGIS combat system engineering agent, under NAVSEA. PE 0604307N Surface Combatant Combat System Engineering is the RDT&E line that funds AEGIS baseline development, integration and fielding, and the appropriation mix corroborates it: 57% of the obligation is RDT&E (Navy) across FY24 and FY23, with 43% O&M (Navy) against the in-service sustainment portion. The name collides with 'AEGIS Combat System (ACS)' at BLI 5231 (Ship Missile Support Equipment), but 5231 is an Other Procurement line and this action obligates no OPN at all, which is the discriminator between the two owners. The O&M share is the one exposure worth a refute pass.

refute_a.reason: The majority of the obligation is RDT&E (Navy) — FY24 $10,784,514 plus FY23 $2,419,697 against FY24 O&M $10,994,304 — and the named scope 'Baseline 10 System Integration and Fielding' plus product documentation is development-and-fielding work that PE 0604307N (Surface Combatant Combat System Engineering) owns; the AEGIS combat system is the program this line funds rather than a platform the contract merely supports, and the PE is a named engineering line, not a rollup, so the 44% in-service-sustainment O&M share is a real minority exposure but does not break the money-and-mission test.

refute_b.reason: The index does hold a verbatim twin — 'AEGIS Combat System (ACS)' at BLI 5231 (Ship Missile Support Equipment) — but the evidence does not link there equally well: 5231 is an Other Procurement line and this paragraph obligates no procurement dollar at all (53% RDT&E Navy across FY24/FY23, 43% O&M), so 0604307N is the only exact-name owner whose colour the paragraph carries; 'Baseline 10' does not name 0604501N's 'AEGIS Capability Build (ACB)' (no 'ACB' or 'Capability Build' string appears), and the alias is not merely a contractor name.

proposals.announcement_evidence: modification to previously awarded contract N00024-23-C-5123 for in-service AEGIS sustainment, system integration, and product documentation and support
proposals.lexicon_quote: The AEGIS Combat System (ACS)	0604307N	340	Surface Combatant Combat System Engineering
proposals.rationale: Same contract as record 35 (N00024-23-C-5123), a later option exercise, but this paragraph says only 'AEGIS' rather than spelling out the combat system, so the basis is alias rather than exact name. The scope — in-service AEGIS sustainment, system integration, and product documentation — is the combat system engineering work PE 0604307N funds, and the appropriation is dominated by RDT&E (75.63% FY25 RDT&E, 24.37% FY19 shipbuilding and conversion), which again excludes the Other Procurement owner of the same name at BLI 5231. Contractor and place of performance (Lockheed Martin Rotary and Mission Systems, Moorestown) match the AEGIS combat system engineering agent. Weaker than record 35 on the name alone; the appropriation and the shared PIID carry it.

refute_a.reason: There is no O&M in this action at all: 75.63% is FY25 RDT&E, the colour PE 0604307N carries, and the 24.37% FY19 shipbuilding-and-conversion minority buys new-construction combat-system content rather than moving the action out of the line; 'system integration and product documentation and support' on the same Moorestown combat-system-engineering contract is the line's own work, and AEGIS here is the combat system itself, not a platform the contract supports.

refute_b.reason: This paragraph's only name evidence is the bare token 'AEGIS', which in this very index is a family owned by at least three PEs — 0604307N (ACS/AWS/AMOD/ADS/CP), 0604501N 'AEGIS Capability Build (ACB)' and 5231 'AEGIS Combat System (ACS)' / 'AEGIS Weapon System (AWS)' — and unlike record 35 it names no combat system, baseline or build to break the tie, while its 24.37% FY19 shipbuilding-and-conversion share points at hull end-cost rather than at the RDT&E line; the shared PIID is contract identity, not name identity, and lens B defaults to refuted when the alias cannot pick its owner.

proposals.announcement_evidence: for AEGIS combat systems engineering, computer program development, in-country support, technical manuals, integrated logistics support, and staging for the Australian air warfare destroyer (AWD) shipbuilding program in support of AEGIS foreign military sales (FMS)

proposals.announcement_evidence: for the procurement of engineering services for development, integration, testing, and logistic support of the Torpedo Warning System.
proposals.lexicon_quote: Torpedo Warning System (TWS)	0603506N	340	Surface Ship Torpedo Defense
proposals.rationale: 'Torpedo Warning System' appears verbatim, twice, and the announcement then defines it in the PE's own terms — detecting threat torpedoes so surface ships can employ hard and soft kill countermeasures — which is the Surface Ship Torpedo Defense mission, not a platform the contract merely supports. The work is 'development, integration, testing, and logistic support', i.e. RDT&E-character effort on a NAVSEA development contract (N00024-11-C-6287) awarded in 2011 and modified here, which is what PE 0603506N funds. refute_a.reason: The scope verbs are development, integration and testing on a 2011 NAVSEA development contract for a system that never reached production, which is RDT&E-character work, and the paragraph restates PE 0603506N's own mission verbatim (detect threat torpedoes, employ hard and soft kill countermeasures), so TWS is the program the line funds rather than a platform it supports and the PE is narrow rather than a catch-all; the unstated appropriation of the $6,200,000 / $2,728,000 and the 'logistic support' tail are residual exposures, but nothing visible in the record places the money outside the development line.

refute_b.reason: 'Torpedo Warning System (TWS)' is owned verbatim by a DIFFERENT PE in this same index — BLI 3113 (doc 342, program title 'SSTD') — and the two owners are near-duplicates of one another (both also carry 'Surface Ship Torpedo Defense (SSTD)', 'Countermeasure Anti-Torpedo (CAT)' and 'AN/SLQ-25'), so the name evidence cannot pick between them; the paragraph never states the colour of the $6,200,000 / $2,728,000 obligated, and 'procurement of engineering services for ... logistic support' reads toward the procurement owner as easily as toward the development one, leaving the identity genuinely undetermined.

proposals.announcement_evidence: The equipment under this contract is in support of the DDG 91 modernization program.

The refutable point is whether AC plant replacement belongs to DDG Mod or to a separate ship-alteration line; nothing in the index offers a competing owner for 'DDG modernization'.

refute_a.reason: 'Fiscal 2024 other procurement (Navy)' does not discriminate this line from its neighbours — BLI 0900 (DDG Mod), BLI 0200 (Surface Combatant HM&E) and BLI 5231 are all OPN rows in this same index — and high-efficiency super-capacity air conditioning plants are HM&E hardware that none of BLI 0900's own named items covers, while BLI 0200 owns the Thermal Management Control System and Class Common Equipment; the announcement's own words are that the equipment 'is in support of the DDG 91 modernization program', i.e. hardware bought in support of one hull's modernization, which is platform-support phrasing rather than evidence that DDG Mod's own procurement line paid for it.

refute_b.reason: No competing owner exists: 'DDG Modernization (DDG MOD) Program' appears at BLI 0900 and nowhere else in the index, and the alias is real rather than invented — 'the DDG 91 modernization program' is the DDG Mod program of record executed on an in-service DDG-51-class hull, not a new-construction buy that BLI 2122 'DDG-51' (SCN) would own, which the fiscal 2024 other-procurement obligation corroborates; the nearest HM&E alternatives ('Thermal Management Control System' at 0200, 'Machinery Alteration (MACHALT)' at 0981) do not name air conditioning plants and 0981 is a catch-all the loader excludes anyway. Whether 'in support of' makes this platform support rather than program content is lens A's question, not identity.

proposals.announcement_evidence: to exercise options for Planar Array Antenna Assembly production requirements to support the Cooperative Engagement Capability program
proposals.lexicon_quote: Planar Array Antenna Assembly (PAAA)	2606	333	Cooperative Engagement Capability
proposals.rationale: The strongest candidate in the chunk. 'Planar Array Antenna Assembly' appears verbatim and is a unique name in this index — only BLI 2606 owns it — and the announcement independently names the owning program, 'the Cooperative Engagement Capability program', in the same sentence. The action is production of that hardware, not services supporting a platform, and it is a NAVSEA option exercise with Raytheon at Largo and McKinney, the CEC hardware sites. The point a refute pass should test is appropriation: the obligation is shipbuilding and conversion (Navy) for FY24 and FY23 rather than the Other Procurement colour BLI 2606 normally carries, because CEC sets for ships under construction are bought in the hull's end cost; 11% of the action is also Japan FMS. Neither changes what the work is — CEC's own antenna production — but both are honest exposures. Note 'Procures Cooperative Engagement Capability (CEC)' also appears at BLI 0900 (DDG Mod); proposing PAAA rather than CEC avoids that collision.

refute_a.reason: The action obligates none of this line's appropriation: BLI 2606 is an Other Procurement (Navy) line (lexicon_doc 333, the OPN book), while the entire US obligation here is shipbuilding and conversion (Navy) — 55% FY24 plus 33% FY23 — and the residual $2,735,089 is 11.03% of the award, matching the stated Japan FMS share exactly, so these PAAA sets are bought inside the hulls' end cost and paid for with SCN and foreign funds, not with the OPN CEC line's money; mission fit is exact but the money test is the one lens A applies, and it fails outright.

refute_b.reason: 'Planar Array Antenna Assembly (PAAA)' is a unique name in this index — only BLI 2606 owns it — and the announcement independently names its owning program, 'the Cooperative Engagement Capability program', in the same sentence; the other CEC-bearing rows (0303138N 'CEC Increment II', 0604234N 'E-2D Cooperative Engagement Capability (CEC)', 0900 'Procures Cooperative Engagement Capability (CEC)') are a different increment, a different platform's set and a destroyer modernization line respectively, and none of them owns PAAA, so this evidence does not link equally well anywhere else. The shipbuilding-and-conversion colour is an appropriation exposure for lens A, not an identity one.

proposals.announcement_evidence: the procurement of urgent spares, containers, and materials in support of refurbishment required to repair Air Intercept Missile (AIM)-9X Tactical and Captive Air Training Missiles (CATMs)
proposals.lexicon_quote: AIM-9X Block II Sidewinder	2209	342	Sidewinder
proposals.rationale: The announcement spells the designator out as 'Air Intercept Missile (AIM)-9X' rather than the index's 'AIM-9X', hence designator-variant rather than exact name, and it later names Block 2 content the row carries explicitly ('one Block 2 PSS ... 19 Block 2 EUs'). The content bought is the missile's own materiel, not services around a platform: active optical target detectors, RF data links, tactical and CATM guidance units, propulsion steering sections and all-up-round containers, all for the Navy, on a fixed-price-incentive-firm action with Raytheon Missile Systems at Tucson. That is Sidewinder program hardware, which the weapons procurement line BLI 2209 funds, rather than the RDT&E line 0207161N (Tactical AIM Missiles) that owns the bare 'AIM-9X' name. Two exposures for the refute lenses: the action mixes Block I and Block 2 articles while the index row names Block II only, and this paragraph does not state the appropriation of the $20,340,987 / $8,275,324 obligated, so a spares-and-refurbishment buy funded from O&M rather than procurement would break it.

refute_a.reason: The buy is 'urgent spares, containers, and materials in support of refurbishment required to repair' already-fielded AIM-9X tactical and CATM rounds — guidance units, AOTD containers, all-up-round containers, a Block I propulsion steering section — which is sustainment and repair content that this same index assigns to 'AIM-9 | 6120 | Spares and Repair Parts', not to BLI 2209, whose narrative procures all-up Sidewinder rounds; the paragraph never states the appropriation of the $20,340,987 / $8,275,324, so nothing rules out O&M or spares money attached to a weapons-procurement line, which is precisely the failure mode lens A hunts.

refute_b.reason: A different PE in this index owns the name and fits the evidence better: BLI 6120 'Spares and Repair Parts' owns 'AIM-9', and this award is literally 'urgent spares, containers, and materials in support of refurbishment required to repair' AIM-9X rounds — spares is the whole scope, so the evidence links at least equally well to 6120, with bare 'AIM-9X' at 0207161N a third owner; on top of that the action is a different variant mix from the row proposed, procuring 'one Block I propulsion steering section' alongside Block 2 articles and CATM guidance units while the row names 'AIM-9X Block II Sidewinder' only.
